capability: Single-phase Darcy flow and Theis drawdown

convergence.note: The dominant error is temporal, not spatial: at fixed nx the max deviation over the window falls 0.055, 0.028, 0.011 as dt halves.

source_strength.how_established: PorousFlowBasicTHM here runs with multiply_by_density = false, so the PorousFlowSquarePulsePointSource mass_flux enters the volume equation directly. The two candidate readings were tested against the drawdown: taken as volumetric it gives a ratio of 0.997 to the closed form, taken as a mass rate divided by density it is off by a factor of 981. The volumetric reading is the one the code implements.

storage_and_transmissivity.note: Recovered separately, not only as the ratio. The prefactor Q/(4 pi T) fixes T because Q is known and independently confirmed; the E1 argument then fixes Ss.

theis_diagnostic.square_domain_seed: theis1.i is retained as a Darcy units sanity check only (delta-p = 4e8 Pa against its analytic 4e8) and carries no Theis acceptance; its finite square boundary is too close.

notes: Axisymmetric Theis drawdown at t = 1000 s on a 1000 m radial domain. Over 2 m < r < 60 m the maximum relative deviation from the closed form is 0.0111 against the declared 2%, with a median of 0.0026. The residual was timestep, not identifiability: the maximum deviation falls 0.0452 at dt=40, 0.0226 at dt=20, 0.0111 at dt=10. Transmissivity and storage are recovered separately by a two-parameter fit, giving T = 1.001e-11 against 1e-11 (0.00147) and Ss = 2.507e-11 against 2.5e-11 (0.00266); their ratio is 0.3995 m^2/s against the exact 0.4. The outer boundary carries 0.00e+00 of the near-well drawdown, so the infinite-aquifer assumption holds.
limitations: Single phase, constant properties, fully saturated, no gravity, rigid skeleton beyond the constant Biot modulus, and unit thickness. The Theis comparison is at one time only; the early-time and Cooper-Jacob late-time regimes are not separately verified. The square-domain seed remains a units check, not a Theis case.
